content.text:
**`createSibling` is now a pure factory.** The old version set `child.keyCount = minDegree - 1` as a hidden side effect — nothing in the name or signature hinted at the mutation. A reader calling `createSibling(child)` had no reason to expect `child` to be modified. Moving the truncation to `splitChild` makes the mutation explicit and local: the caller that owns the split operation is now visibly responsible for truncating the child.

**`BTree.insert()` separates two independent concerns.** The old null branch did two things — ensure the root exists, then insert — folded together in a single `if` arm. The else branch also inserted, meaning the same `root.insert(key)` call appeared twice (once explicitly in the null arm, once in the else). The new version initialises the root independently (if needed), then unconditionally runs the capacity check. Each `if` now has one job.
